claim: BPD showed a strong positive genetic correlation with PTSD.
primary_limit: Comorbidity, symptom overlap, and diagnostic misclassification cannot be fully disentangled.

claim: BPD showed a strong positive genetic correlation with depression.
primary_limit: Shared genetic liability does not establish causal direction.

claim: BPD showed a strong positive genetic correlation with ADHD.
primary_limit: Shared genetic liability does not establish causal direction.

claim: The combined analysis identified 11 independent associated genomic loci.
primary_limit: A significant locus is not equivalent to a single causal gene.

claim: Gene-based analysis implicated nine genes.
primary_limit: Gene-level association does not by itself establish a causal molecular mechanism.

claim: SNP heritability was estimated at 17.3% on the liability scale.
primary_limit: SNP heritability is not equivalent to total heritability or individual determinism.

claim: BPD polygenic scores predicted 4.6% of phenotypic variance on the liability scale.
primary_limit: Research-level prediction does not imply clinical diagnostic utility.

claim: BPD-PGS was associated with psychiatric and somatic phecodes in BioVU and UK Biobank.
population: BioVU and UK Biobank target samples
primary_limit: PheWAS associations may reflect shared genetic risk and do not establish that BPD causes somatic disease.

claim: The discovery GWAS included 12,339 BPD cases and 1,041,717 controls.
primary_limit: Large sample size does not eliminate phenotype heterogeneity or ancestry limitations.

claim: Independent replication datasets included 685 cases and 107,750 controls.
primary_limit: Replication remains within the ancestry scope of the study.

claim: The discovery GWAS identified six independent genome-wide significant loci.
primary_limit: Genome-wide significance does not establish biological causality.

claim: All six genome-wide significant lead SNPs showed effects in the same direction in replication.
primary_limit: Directional replication is supportive but is not equivalent to exact effect-size replication.

claim: Among lead SNPs with discovery P<1e-6, 24 of 31 showed effects in the same direction in replication.
primary_limit: Directional concordance should not be rewritten as universal replication of every association.

claim: Female liability-scale SNP heritability was estimated at 20.5%.
primary_limit: Sex-stratified estimates depend on prevalence assumptions and unequal statistical power.

claim: Male liability-scale SNP heritability was estimated at 10.2%.
primary_limit: The male analysis had substantially fewer cases and lower power.

claim: Female-only and male-only GWAS showed a high genetic correlation.
primary_limit: The correlation did not significantly differ from 1 (z=-1.60; P=0.055).

claim: The female-only analysis identified rs73581580 in the EXD3 locus.
primary_limit: Variant association does not establish an EXD3 causal mechanism.

claim: The female-only analysis identified rs10227454 near the FOXP2 locus.
primary_limit: Proximity to FOXP2 does not establish FOXP2 as the causal gene.

claim: The male-only analysis identified rs17757829 on chromosome 2.
primary_limit: The male-only analysis was smaller and lower-powered.

claim: The male-only analysis identified rs6032676 on chromosome 20.
primary_limit: The male-only analysis was smaller and lower-powered.

claim: After excluding bipolar disorder or schizophrenia, FOXP2 rs4727799 and EXD3 rs73581580 were the only main-analysis loci remaining genome-wide significant.
primary_limit: Sensitivity analysis reduces one source of comorbidity but does not eliminate all diagnostic overlap.

claim: The S1P-S1P3 pathway was the only gene set significant after multiple-testing correction.
primary_limit: Pathway enrichment does not establish that this pathway causally mediates BPD.

claim: Cerebellar tissue showed the strongest nominal GTEx tissue enrichment but was not significant after correction.
primary_limit: All adjusted P values were >0.32; nominal enrichment must not be presented as corrected significance.

claim: Genes expressed in medium spiny neurons showed significant SNP-heritability enrichment.
population: Human Brain Atlas single-nucleus RNA-seq annotations
primary_limit: Enrichment indicates concentration of heritability, not a proven cellular causal mechanism.

claim: Genes expressed in LAMP5-LHX6 and Chandelier cells showed significant SNP-heritability enrichment.
population: Human Brain Atlas single-nucleus RNA-seq annotations
primary_limit: Enrichment indicates concentration of heritability, not a proven cellular causal mechanism.

claim: In the Spain 2 replication sample, PGS explained 3.1% of variance and achieved AUC 62.4%.
primary_limit: This level of prediction does not establish clinical diagnostic utility.

claim: In the All of Us replication sample, PGS explained 2.6% of variance and achieved AUC 61.4%.
primary_limit: Statistical association and AUC do not by themselves justify clinical screening.

claim: The highest PGS decile had higher BPD case-control odds than the lowest decile.
population: European ancestry individual-level datasets excluding All of Us for merged decile analysis
primary_limit: A group-level odds ratio is not an individual probability or diagnosis.

claim: In BioVU, 69 of 1,431 tested diagnoses were associated with BPD-PGS after Bonferroni correction.
primary_limit: Multiple phenotype associations do not imply BPD causes those diagnoses.

claim: In UK Biobank, 317 of 1,250 tested diagnoses were associated with BPD-PGS after Bonferroni correction.
primary_limit: Associations may reflect shared genetic liability and correlated phenotypes.

claim: Of 56 BioVU-significant diagnoses with sufficient UKB cases, 51 had effects in the same direction and 41 were also significant in UKB.
primary_limit: Cross-biobank consistency does not establish causal mechanisms.

claim: Phecode 301.20 had OR 1.41 in BioVU.
primary_limit: Odds ratio is a population-level association, not an individual diagnosis.

claim: Phecode 301.20 had OR 1.54 in UK Biobank.
primary_limit: Odds ratio is a population-level association, not an individual diagnosis.

claim: None of the 16 genes prioritized from the discovery GWAS were highlighted as drug targets by Open Targets.
population: Prioritized genes from BPD discovery GWAS
primary_limit: Absence of highlighted targets does not establish that the genes are biologically irrelevant or undruggable.

claim: Genome-wide DRUGSETS results did not remain statistically significant after multiple-testing correction.
primary_limit: Biologically plausible drug signals should not be presented as statistically established findings.
